options.game: The Last of Us Part II
options.how: Performance-captured actors, photoreal faces, real-world materials and lighting so violence and grief read as believable.
Hand-drawn, hand-inked 1930s rubber hose cartoon frames over watercolor backgrounds, with film grain and old-reel filters.

sources.note: The Last of Us Part II: PS Blog: motion capture of real actors plus facial animation system aiming for most realistic in-game character rendering
Cuphead: Steam: inspired by 1930s cartoons, traditional hand drawn cel animation, watercolor backgrounds; released Sep 29 2017

options.how: Scanned, licensed real cars and real-world circuits rendered for photoreal accuracy, with a photo mode built around real camera settings.
Cartoon Nintendo characters, toy-like karts and fantasy tracks that flip into anti-gravity, so readability beats realism.

sources.note: Gran Turismo 7: PlayStation page: cars recreated in unparalleled detail, real-life locations, Scapes for realistic photos; released Mar 4 2022
Mario Kart 8: Super Mario Wiki: released May 2014; anti-gravity segments introduced, driving on walls and ceilings

options.how: Realistic licensed player likenesses and real stadiums, presented like a TV broadcast of real matches.
Mushroom Kingdom characters, exaggerated trick shots and glowing zone-shot effects on fantasy courts.

sources.note: EA Sports FC 24: Steam tags Realistic, Simulation, 3D
Mario Tennis Aces: Super Mario Wiki: released June 2018; Zone Shots, Trick Shots, energy gauge, Zone Speed confirmed

options.how: Grounded small-town streets, realistic human faces and lighting, with fog and grain making the plausible feel wrong.
Sumi-e ink wash look with brush outlines and paper texture; the Celestial Brush lets players paint on the screen itself.

sources.note: Silent Hill 2: official page
Okami: Steam: renowned Sumi-e ink art style; copyright 2006 for original. Celestial Brush not stated on this page

options.how: Fighters are digitized video of real actors, giving photographic sprites that made the gore controversial.
Hand-drawn, anime-influenced sprite fighters with exaggerated proportions and expressive animation.

sources.note: Mortal Kombat: official page
Street Fighter II: collection page: key animation sprites, Pixel Graphics and Anime tags

options.how: Pre-rendered 3D stills aiming for photographic plausibility, so the island feels like a real place to examine.
Flat pastel isometric architecture inspired by Escher, where impossible geometry is the visual identity.

sources.note: Myst: official page
Monument Valley: official page

options.how: Recreates the real planet with live traffic and real-time weather, so the world you fly over matches reality.
Cel-shaded characters with thick outlines and graffiti-tag art direction over a stylized Tokyo.

sources.note: Microsoft Flight Simulator: Realistic tag; live traffic and real-time weather
Jet Set Radio: Steam: mark turf with graffiti across Tokyo-to, references original Dreamcast release; cel-shading not stated on page

options.how: Tiny pixel sprites in a three-color palette (palettes unlock), so every frame reads instantly on a phone screen.
Dense photoreal environments, performance capture and detailed character models built by a large AAA team.

sources.note: Downwell: Steam: released Oct 15 2015, Pixel Graphics/Retro tags. Three-color and unlockable palette detail not stated on page
Uncharted 4: A Thief's End: Steam: Uncharted 4 has the largest and most detailed environments in the franchise; PlayStation page lists 05/10/2016 release. Perf capture not stated

options.how: Simple pixel sprites reused in huge numbers, keeping hundreds of enemies and projectiles cheap to draw.
Detailed 3D gothic environments, high-poly monsters and pre-rendered cinematics from a large AAA team.

sources.note: Vampire Survivors: Steam: hundreds of monsters, Pixel Graphics tag; Early Access Dec 17 2021, full Oct 2022
Diablo IV: Official site: dark fantasy action-RPG, Sanctuary regions with incredible graphics. Cinematics and 2023 date not stated on page

options.how: Deliberately low-poly 1990s-style models with crunchy textures and a pixelation option.
High-detail id Tech 7 demons and arenas with detailed gore and destructible demon armor rendering.

sources.note: Dusk: Steam: retro FPS inspired by 90s legends, pixelated gore; released Dec 10 2018. Low-poly not explicitly stated
Doom Eternal: official page

options.how: Chunky low-resolution pixel art for faces and documents, made by a solo developer.
Performance-captured actors with high-detail faces and environments to sell subtle android emotion.

sources.note: Papers, Please: Steam: pixel-art content, document checking, developed by Lucas Pope; released Aug 8 2013
Detroit: Become Human: Quantic Dream: cast of named actors (Jesse Williams, Clancy Brown, Valorie Curry etc), 2018 copyright; perf capture not stated

options.how: Pixel art fighters and stages with limited palettes, animated frame by frame.
Unreal Engine 5 fighters with high-fidelity skin, hair and muscle detail, lifelike animation and heavy dynamic effects.

sources.note: Rivals of Aether: Steam: Pixel Graphics/Retro tags, released Mar 28 2017. Limited palettes not stated on page
Tekken 8: Official site: Powered by Unreal Engine 5, high-fidelity skin, hair and muscles; Steam lists Jan 25 2024. Stage destruction not stated

options.how: Simple stylized cars and stages viewed from a top-down camera, with clean flat-colored low-detail geometry.
Detailed licensed car models across a large, varied Mexico with dense jungles, weekly seasons and dynamic dust and tropical storms.

sources.note: Art of Rally: Steam: stylized experience, colorful stylized environments in top-down view; released Sep 23 2020
Forza Horizon 5: Steam: open world Mexico with jungles and deserts, weekly seasons, dust and tropical storms; released Nov 8 2021. Photogrammetry not stated

options.how: Black and white silhouettes in grey fog with film grain; almost no color at all.
Neon red and blue sabers and blocks against dark stages, with bright light shows.

sources.note: Limbo: Steam tags Dark, Minimalist, Atmospheric
Beat Saber: official page

options.how: Gothic ink-heavy art with dark, desaturated tones and heavy shadow.
Bright saturated pegs, rainbows and fireworks celebrating every big shot.

sources.note: Darkest Dungeon: Steam: striking hand-drawn gothic crowquill art style, ever-encroaching dark; released Jan 19 2016
Peggle: official page

options.how: Dithered 1-bit style black-and-white graphics with minimal color, evoking early monochrome computer games.
Vivid particle effects and color that shift with music in each stage.

sources.note: Return of the Obra Dinn: Steam: An Insurance Adventure with Minimal Color, Kotaku quote on stippled black-and-white graphics; released Oct 18 2018. Early Mac not stated
Tetris Effect: Steam (Connected edition): each stage has its own music, graphical style and background that evolve as you play; original 2018 year not on page

options.how: Dark, near-monochrome greys and blacks; color is rationed so the world stays bleak.
Bright toy-like primary colors on simple low-poly objects and candy-colored worlds.

sources.note: Inside: Steam tags Dark, Minimalist, Atmospheric
Katamari Damacy: REROLL remaster page, Colorful tag

options.how: Dark, desaturated castle interiors lit by a dim lantern, so darkness itself is the dominant color.
Bold painterly orange, pink and teal forest skies that shift with the time of day.

sources.note: Amnesia: The Dark Descent: official page
Firewatch: Steam tag Colorful

options.how: A minimalist text adventure: plain text and buttons on a bare page, with almost no color or art.
Bright cartoon businesses and colorful buttons in a retro-futurist style.

sources.note: A Dark Room: official site: a minimalist text adventure
AdVenture Capitalist: Steam tags Colorful, 2D

options.how: Health is a meter on the RIG suit spine and ammo shows on the gun; menus are holograms projected in the world.
Dense overlay HUD of action bars, unit frames and minimap, extended further by player-made addons.

sources.note: Dead Space: release Oct 24 2008; page review notes health indicator and UI are part of the game world
World of Warcraft: addons augment or replace default UI incl. action bars and unit frames; year not on page

options.how: A wristwatch shows gas mask timer and a light that signals stealth; the mask visor cracks as it takes damage.
Shield and health bars, XP bar and floating damage numbers overlaid on the screen.

sources.note: Metro 2033: official page
Borderlands: official page

options.how: The player holds up a physical map and GPS in hand to navigate; the game keeps running while you look.
Minimap, compass, ammo counter and hit markers all overlay the screen.

sources.note: Far Cry 2: official page
Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare: official page

options.how: The motion tracker is a handheld device the player raises; saving uses in-world emergency phones.
Team health bars on screen and colored outlines of teammates and items through walls.

sources.note: Alien: Isolation: official page
Left 4 Dead: official page

options.how: No HUD: Henry raises a paper map and compass in his hands to navigate, and the game keeps running while he looks.
Minimap with quest markers, health and stamina bars, and buff icons overlay the view.

sources.note: Firewatch: official page
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt: official page

options.how: Healing is a physical act in the world: you inject health syringes or use wall-mounted health stations that jab needles into your hand.
A full HUD of health, armor and ammo counts plus equipment icons, with over 20 options to customize it.

sources.note: Half-Life: Alyx: health syringes and wall-mounted health stations that inject into the back of your fingers
Doom Eternal: customizable HUD with over 20 options

options.how: No HUD: the glowing glyphs on your scarf show how much flight energy you have left.
A status bar at the bottom shows health, armor, ammo and weapons.

sources.note: Journey: official page
Quake: official page

options.how: Hidden DVs and stat experience shape stats but are never shown in game; players had to infer them.
A full character sheet lists every resistance, damage and defense number, with exact item affix values.

sources.note: Pokemon Red and Blue: DVs are not visible to the player; Gen 1 terms are DVs and stat experience, not IVs/EVs
Path of Exile: official page

options.how: Villager friendship is a hidden point value; players read it only through gifts and dialogue.
Nested tooltips break down every modifier behind a value, with ledgers comparing nations.

sources.note: Animal Crossing: New Horizons: friendship is hidden 0-255 value inferred from gifts, dialogue, photos and Katrina
Europa Universalis IV: official page

options.how: Items show only a name and short cryptic tagline on pickup, so players learn effects by experiment or wiki.
The logbook and item descriptions give exact percentages and stacking values for each item.

sources.note: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth: items carry a name and short tagline (e.g. D6 'Reroll your destiny') separate from full effect
Risk of Rain 2: descriptions give exact values e.g. +15% attack speed (+15% per stack); early access was 2019, 1.0 in 2020

options.how: Kart combos show five stat bars, while values like mini-turbo and water, air and anti-gravity speed stay hidden.
Exact horsepower, weight and performance points, with numeric tuning sliders for parts.

sources.note: Mario Kart 8: five stat bars shown; mini-turbo and terrain speeds/handling are hidden stats; invincibility not confirmed
Gran Turismo 7: official page

options.how: No in-game move data; techniques like wavedashing, a physics engine exploit, were discovered by players after release.
Item descriptions give exact values and stacking, such as Soldier's Syringe: +15% attack speed, +15% per extra stack.

sources.note: Super Smash Bros. Melee: wavedash is a physics engine exploit first found by players in 2002
Risk of Rain 2: Increases attack speed by 15% (+15% per stack)

options.how: Rising Insight silently changes the world, adding messengers, enemies and sights at thresholds that players had to map out themselves.
Items roll affixes with exact numeric bonuses (damage, crit chance, resistances) listed on each tooltip.

sources.note: Bloodborne: Insight unlocks and world changes at thresholds
Diablo IV: affixes add stats such as increased damage, critical hit chance and resistances

options.how: Villager friendship is a point value the game never shows; players gauge it through Katrina's fortune readings and villager dialogue.
Each hero's stress is a visible gauge from 0 to 200: at 100 they turn afflicted or virtuous, at 200 they suffer a heart attack.

sources.note: Animal Crossing: New Horizons: friendship points; level read via Katrina and villager dialogue
Darkest Dungeon: stress bar from 0 to 200, affliction check at 100, heart attack at 200

options.how: Almost no music; ambient drones and sound effects carry the mood.
Mick Gordon metal score that ramps up when combat starts and calms when arenas are cleared.

sources.note: Limbo: official page
Doom (2016): official page

options.how: The iMUSE system transitions music seamlessly between locations and characters.
Ambient soundscapes instead of a score, so the player can listen for guards and footsteps.

sources.note: Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge: official page
Thief: The Dark Project: 1998 Looking Glass; players rely on hearing guards, footsteps and noise; ambient score not detailed

options.how: The metal score intensifies as you stay in sync and build fury, so the music grows with how well you play.
An ambient soundtrack and sound design carry the mood instead of melodic themes.

Mostly wind, wildlife and silence, with music used sparingly.

sources.note: Red Dead Redemption: official page
The Long Dark: official page

Sound is information: guards react to noise and players lean on doors to listen, so the soundscape stays sparse.

Thief: The Dark Project: sound travels, guards notice loud noises, players lean on doors to listen

Ambient soundscape of creaks, wind and distant noises instead of a melodic score.

sources.note: Alien: Isolation: official page
Darkwood: official page

options.how: The score follows the player's movement and progress, swelling at key moments.
No music at all; only environmental sounds accompany the puzzles.

options.how: Every move and attack must land on the beat of the song; missing the beat costs your multiplier.
Blocks fly at the player in time with the music and are sliced on the beat in VR.
Binaural voices and sound build the experience, but combat and puzzles are not timed to music.

Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice: review: voices swirl around the player in 3D binaural audio

Doom (2016): fast, fluid movement and intense first-person combat with no cover

options.how: Any song from your library generates a track whose blocks and slopes follow the music.
Licensed radio stations play while you drive; the music never shapes the track, timing or scoring.

sources.note: Tetris Effect: music, backgrounds and sounds pulse in perfect sync with how you are playing
